Codes, readiness monitors and freeze frame. This takes several seconds on a K-line car. Keep the ignition on.

The read did not finish. Check that the ignition is on and the adapter is connected, then read again.
Codes cleared. The readiness monitors start over and need a drive cycle before they are ready again.
The connection dropped while clearing. Read again to see what is left.
Codes can only be cleared with the ignition on and the engine off. Stop the engine, leave the ignition on, wait until RPM shows 0 and tap Clear codes again.
The stored and pending codes, the freeze frame and the readiness monitors are erased. The check-engine light goes off.
The monitors need a drive cycle before they are ready again. If the fault is still there, the codes come back.
This erases the codes, the freeze frame and the readiness monitors, and it cannot be undone. Only continue if you are sure.
Not connected and no GPS fix. Connect under Setup, Connection, or wait for the GPS.

Switch the adapter on and tap Scan. A Konnwei KW905 needs its button pressed so the LED is on.

Android night mode, often set by the headlights
How the main page shows engine speed, road speed and coolant. Theme default follows the theme in effect.
Reconnect when the unit wakes up
Opening the dashboard on its own needs \"Display over other apps\", which is not allowed yet.
The head unit announces ignition on and off with a broadcast. The time shows when each one last reached the app, so you can see which one your unit sends.
Type the action of the broadcast first.
That action is too long (maximum length %1$s).
Use letters, digits, dots and underscores only.
That action is already in the list.

Many units force-stop apps about 20 to 30 seconds after the ignition goes off, and a stopped app gets no broadcasts until you open it by hand. Add K-Line Dash to the sleep whitelist in the factory settings (Settings, then the factory menu; the code 8888 is common but differs per firmware). Newer firmware has no list there: use the FYT Factory tool instead. Open the app once after changing the list.

Add K-Line Dash to the list of programs that may run after sleep: \"Whitelist of programs to run after sleep\" in the Malaysk ROM, or the BootControl app on Microntek firmware. Open the app once by hand afterwards.

Look in the settings of the unit itself for autostart, a sleep whitelist or a do-not-kill list and add K-Line Dash. Many units stop the app when the ignition goes off, and it only comes back when you open it by hand. Then allow background running with the buttons below.
Battery optimization is off for this app.
Battery optimization is on for this app. Allow background running below.
This head unit has no screen for that setting. Use the settings of the unit itself instead.
Car off. Waiting for the unit to wake up.
RPM bar, three big fields, six small ones
2 to 9 cells, each a number or a graph
Big RPM, shift light, peak hold
Tap a field to choose its signal.
Tap a cell to choose its signal and whether it shows a number or a graph.
The RPM bar and the frame of the page flash from the shift point.
Not connected, so every signal is listed. The ones the car does not report stay empty.
No tracks yet. Start a lap session and set the start/finish line on the road.
Drive across the line at a steady speed and tap when you pass it.
Choose a format. The files are made from the trip and its track as they are now.
Get them off the head unit with the Wi-Fi export or Copy to USB on the Trips page.
This trip has no GPS data, so there is no route.
Could not read this lap. Select it again.
The simulated car drives a 2 km circuit at the speed of the simulator, so laps can be timed without a car.
No tracks yet. Start a lap session on the Trips page and set the start/finish line while driving.
USE chooses the track for the next lap session. ACTIVE switches lap timing off again.
Renaming opens the keyboard, so it is off while the car moves. USE chooses the track for the next lap session.
Metric: km/h, km, °C, kPa, litres. Imperial: mph, miles, °F, psi, US gallons. Exports to a PC stay metric.
Connect your adapter to see live data
Plug an OBD2 adapter into your car, then set it up here. It takes about two minutes.
No adapter yet? The simulator drives a virtual car.
Your car, live on one screen
K-Line Dash shows speed, RPM, temperatures and more, straight from the car.
All you need is an OBD2 adapter in the car and this device.
Setup takes about two minutes. You can skip it at any step.
Works offline. No account. No data leaves your device unless you export it.
The most common kind. It came with a PIN like 1234 or 0000.
Newer adapters, often sold as BLE or Bluetooth 4.0. No PIN.
The adapter makes its own Wi-Fi network.
No adapter yet: try the simulator
A virtual car, so you can look around the app first.
Not sure? If your adapter came with a PIN like 1234, choose Bluetooth.
Plug the adapter into the OBD port of the car and switch the ignition on. The engine can stay off.
Pair it in the Bluetooth settings of Android. The PIN is usually 1234, 0000 or 6789.
Come back here and choose the adapter from the list.
If the adapter has a button, press it. Its light should come on.
Tap Scan and choose the adapter from the list.
Join the Wi-Fi network of the adapter. It has no internet, which is normal.
Check the address. Most adapters use 192.168.0.10 and port 35000.
Android will ask to allow \"Nearby devices\". K-Line Dash only uses it to find your adapter.
Android will ask to allow \"Location\". This Android version needs it to find Bluetooth devices. K-Line Dash only uses it to find your adapter.
This unit has no screen for that. Open the settings of the unit itself.
The first connection can take up to 30 seconds while the app finds out how your car talks.
Asking the car which sensors it has…
This is the simulator, a virtual car. Connect a real adapter later under Setup, Connection.
This adapter does not work with K-Line Dash
It only talks to its own app. Choose another adapter, or try the simulator. These adapters work:
The adapter works, but the car stays silent. Turn the ignition on (the engine may stay off) and try again. Also check that the adapter sits all the way in the OBD port.
K-Line Dash needs the permission \"Nearby devices\" to reach the adapter. Tap Allow Bluetooth. If Android does not ask again, turn it on under Settings, Apps, K-Line Dash, Permissions.
Pair the adapter in the Bluetooth settings of Android (PIN 1234, 0000 or 6789), then choose it in the list and try again.
Press the button on the adapter so its light is on, then tap Scan and choose the adapter.
Join the Wi-Fi network of the adapter in the Wi-Fi settings of Android, check the address and try again.
Turn Bluetooth on and try again.
No Bluetooth for apps on this unit
This head unit does not let apps use its Bluetooth. Use a Wi-Fi adapter instead.
Check that the adapter is plugged into the OBD port, the ignition is on and the adapter is paired (PIN 1234, 0000 or 6789). If it has a button, press it. Then try again.
Check that the adapter is plugged in and the ignition is on. Press its button so the light is on, and close other OBD apps: an adapter talks to one app at a time. Then try again.
Unplug the adapter, plug it back in, wait for its light and try again. A loose OBD port can cause this.
Check the adapter and the ignition, then try again. Setup, Debug shows what the adapter says.
A trip is saved while the engine runs. You can delete trips on the Trips page.
Allow location to see GPS speed, record routes and time laps. It stays on this device.
Allow notifications so Android shows that the connection to the adapter stays alive in the background.
Live values. Swipe left or right for more pages.
Everything your car reports, with how often it updates.
Answers to common problems, and this setup if you want to run it again.
Plug the adapter into the OBD port of the car. It is usually under the dashboard on the driver\'s side. Switch the ignition on. The engine can stay off.

Pair the adapter in the Bluetooth settings of Android first (PIN 1234, 0000 or 6789). Then open Setup, Connection, choose Bluetooth Classic and pick the adapter. Adapters that look like OBD adapters are listed first.
Press the button on the adapter if it has one. Choose Bluetooth LE, tap Scan and pick the adapter. These adapters need no PIN.

Join the Wi-Fi network of the adapter in the Wi-Fi settings of Android. It has no internet, which is normal. Choose Wi-Fi in Setup, Connection and check the address: most adapters use 192.168.0.10, port 35000.
Tap Connect. The first connection to a car can take up to 30 seconds while the app finds the right protocol; later ones are faster. The dot in the bottom bar turns green and Dash shows live values.
Choose Simulator in Setup, Connection to try the app with a virtual car.
The adapter is not in the list

A Bluetooth Classic adapter must be paired in the Bluetooth settings of Android first. Pair it, come back and tap Refresh. For Bluetooth LE, press the button on the adapter if it has one, then tap Scan; the light must be on. Some adapters sleep when the ignition is off: switch the ignition on and plug the adapter in again.

Switch the ignition on; the engine may stay off. Push the adapter all the way into the OBD port. If values stay empty, tap Forget protocol in Setup, Connection and connect again. Setup, Debug shows what the adapter and the car say, which helps when you ask for help.
Some adapters only work with their own app, for example BlueDriver, ThinkDiag, Golo, TopScan, ANCEL and Autel. K-Line Dash cannot use them. See Supported adapters for adapters that work.
Values update slowly on an older car

That is normal. Cars with a K-line connection (mostly cars built before 2008) answer about two requests per second in total, so every extra value slows the others. Newer cars with CAN are much faster. Dash only asks for what is on screen: a page with fewer fields updates faster.
The head unit closes the app after the ignition goes off

Many head units stop apps shortly after the ignition is switched off. Add K-Line Dash to the sleep whitelist of the unit and allow background running. Setup, Startup explains how for FYT / UIS and Microntek units. Open the app once by hand afterwards.

GPS needs the location permission (Setup, GPS and Tracks, Allow location), the location switch of Android on, and a clear view of the sky. The first fix can take a few minutes. Some head units have no GPS antenna connected; trips then record from the adapter only, without a route or laps.

Automatic recording starts when the engine runs and the adapter is connected, and ends two minutes after the engine stops. Without an adapter, switch on \"When the car moves\" on the Trips page: it starts above 10 km/h (6 mph) with a GPS fix. Check that the switch is on and that the unit has free storage.
K-Line Dash speaks plain ELM327, so an adapter that works with other generic OBD apps usually works here too. These are known to work:

The cheap \"ELM327 v1.5\" and \"v2.1\" adapters work, but some do not answer every optional command; the app skips those. Pair a Bluetooth Classic clone first. A Konnwei KW905 only works over Bluetooth LE. Adapters with an STN chip or newer ELM327 firmware are the best choice for cars from 2008 on.

Adapters that only talk to their own app: BlueDriver, ThinkDiag, Launch Golo and EasyDiag, TOPDON TopScan, ANCEL BD200 and Autel MaxiAP. K-Line Dash then reports Adapter not supported. FIXD is not verified.
Open Trips and wait until GPS in the bottom bar turns green. It needs the location permission.
Tap Start lap session, or Start lap timing during a trip that already runs.
Drive across the line at a steady speed, faster than walking pace, and tap Set start/finish here as you pass it. The GPS must be accurate to 15 m or better.
Tap Add sector here at each point where you want a split time. A sector line does not restart the lap clock.
Current lap, last lap, best lap and the delta to your best show on Trips. A green delta means you are ahead of your best lap.
Open the trip in the Trips list for the lap table, the route and graphs of speed and RPM. The track is saved under Setup, GPS and Tracks and offered again for your next session.
Open a trip on the Trips page and tap Export for PC. Choose a format. Lap sessions also give a CSV with one row per lap.
VBO: Circuit Tools, RaceChrono and RaceRender. GPX: Google Earth, GPS Visualizer and most map apps. CSV: Excel, LibreOffice Calc and Google Sheets.
Get the files off the unit
Use Copy to USB or SD card on the Trips page. Or tap Start Wi-Fi export and open the address it shows in a browser on a phone or PC on the same network, then type the PIN shown on the unit.
Exports are always metric (km/h, km, °C), as the VBO and GPX formats expect, whatever units the app shows. The CSV column names include the unit, for example speed (km/h).

An adapter draws power from the OBD port all the time. Simple adapters use roughly 20 to 50 mA and have no sleep mode, so the ignition does not switch them off. Better ones (OBDLink, Vgate iCar Pro and vLinker) sleep when the engine stops and use only a few mA.
Unplug a simple adapter when the car stands for more than a week or two, or when the battery is already weak.
While the engine is off, K-Line Dash stops asking the car for values (the status bar says Engine off). Set a battery warning under Setup, Warnings to hear about a low voltage early.
Made for drivers who want to see what their car is doing.
K-Line Dash works offline. It has no account, no ads and no analytics, and it sends nothing anywhere. Your trips, settings and crash reports stay on this device until you export them yourself.
Finds your Bluetooth adapter and talks to it.
Only for GPS speed, routes and lap times, and on Android 11 and older to find Bluetooth LE adapters. It never leaves the device.
Shows that the connection to the adapter stays alive in the background.
Reaches a Wi-Fi adapter, and serves your trips to your own devices on the same network during the optional Wi-Fi export. That export is off until you start it and needs a PIN.
Only if you turn them on
Start with the head unit, display over other apps and the battery optimization exemption, all under Setup, Startup.
K-Line Dash is built with these open-source libraries. Test-only tools such as JUnit are not part of the app.
A report holds the error and the app version, nothing else. Nothing is sent: share the file yourself if you report a problem.
